Editor restored final letter ⲩ (3pl. suffix) in ⲁⲭⲱ[ⲩ]. Translator reads ⲁⲭⲱⲩ as Lyc. ⲉϫⲱⲟⲩ 'upon them' (with ⲭ for ϫ); idiom ϣⲱⲡⲉ + ⲉϫⲱ⸗ = 'happen upon, befall.' Hence 'becoming-upon-them' = befalling them. Tentative.
Editor restored initial letter ⲉ in [ⲉ]ⲧⲃⲉ; standard Coptic preposition 'because of, therefore' opens the paraenetic exhortation. Whole word treated as restored unit.
Editor restored ⲛⲧⲁ at line 24 start; standard Coptic temporal converter ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲣⲉ = 'when (perfective)' opens the disciples' reaction-narrative. Common Kephalaia formula closing chapter.

notes.decision: Both are Lycopolitan action-nouns formed with the ⲟ̄ⲓⲛ-/ⲟ̄ⲓ- nominalizing prefix (cf. ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲃⲱⲗ 'dissolution,' ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛ†ⲟⲩⲱ 'raising' in glossary): 'his shining-forth' (ⲡⲣⲓⲉ — same root as ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ 'the Radiance') and 'his setting' (ϩⲱⲧⲡ̄, said of the sun). The contrast preserves the active-emission semantics of ⲡⲣⲓⲉ per terminology guide.

Read as ⲥⲱⲧ + ⲛ̄ⲍⲱⲱⲩ 'draw themselves' (ⲥⲱⲧ akin to ⲥⲱⲕ 'pull, draw'; ⲭⲱⲩ as Lyc. reflex of reflexive ϩⲱⲟⲩ 'themselves,' cf. ⲍⲱⲱϩ noted in dialect entries). The creatures of flesh draw themselves out of sleep at sunrise.

ⲧⲟⲛⲱ = Lycopolitan ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raising' (per terminology guide must preserve vertical/upward semantics). The day-mystery IS named 'a great Raising-up' — the sun's morning re-emergence is correspondentially the cosmic raising of light. Capitalized to mark the technical Manichaean register.

Read as the directional infinitive ⲁ-ϣⲁⲣϣⲣ̄, with ϣⲁⲣϣⲣ̄/ϣⲣ̄ϣⲣ̄ a reduplicated form related to the scattering/breaking root underlying ⲭⲣⲁⲣⲁⲧ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'scattered forth' in the glossary. In Manichaean correspondential terms, humans coming forth at dawn 'scatter upon' (= work, cut, harvest) the Cross of Light — Jesus patibilis enduring suffering through their daily activity.

ⲡⲧⲏϩ from ⲧⲱϩ 'mix, join, match' substantivized = 'the matching, the corresponding-to.' The construction ⲉⲣⲉ ⲡⲉⲓ̈ ⲡⲧⲏϩ ⲁ- = 'this matches/corresponds to.' Standard Manichaean correspondential identifier.

Translated 'the Election itself.' ⲧⲧⲥⲁⲧⲧ is feminine substantival 'the chosen-one/election' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲥⲁⲧⲧ as masc. epithet of Zarathustra) with ⲍⲱⲱϩ = Lyc. ϩⲱⲱⲥ 'itself.' The doubled article ⲧ-ⲧⲥⲁⲧⲧ marks the substantival use. Functions here as the cosmic Election-event referenced in the eschatological sun-typology.

Parsed as ⲉϥ-ϯ-ⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'which gives the sign' — verbal idiom ϯⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ already in glossary as the agent-noun ⲣⲉϥϯⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'sign-giver.' The mystery of the end 'gives the sign' at the cosmic consummation — fits the chapter's overall correspondence-revelation theme.

Translated 'depiction of fullness.' ⲙⲁϩ taken as Lyc. reflex of ⲙⲉϩ (qualitative of ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fill') = 'fullness, fulness.' The 'depiction of fullness' = the eschatological Last Statue / cosmic Image filled with the gathered Light. Alternative reading 'depiction of truth' (ⲙⲏⲉ) also possible but less likely morphologically.

Recurring noun (lines 12, 14) translated 'the sunless place.' Analyzed as ⲧⲙ̄- (privative) + ⲡⲣⲉ/ⲡⲣⲏ ('sun') = 'place without sun.' Context (paired with ⲡⲙⲁⲛ̄ⲱⲡⲧ 'place of judgment,' ⲧⲟⲩⲱⲏ ⲛ̄ⲕⲉⲕⲉ 'night of darkness,' and Death's destination) supports a hellish/dark register. Notably this passage immediately precedes Kephalaion 67's sun-typology, making the 'sunless' reading thematically apt. Tentative — alternative readings 'fruitless place' (ⲡⲣⲉ = ⲡⲣⲏⲉ 'fruit') or 'kingless place' also possible.

Translated 'this Illuminator who radiates.' Parsed ⲉⲡⲡⲣⲓⲉ as relative ⲉⲧ-ⲡⲣⲓⲉ 'who radiates' (with Lyc. ⲡ for ⲧⲡ assimilation). Preserves the active verbal-emission semantics of ⲡⲣⲓⲉ 'shine forth' (same root as ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ 'the Radiance' in glossary). Alternative reading as title 'the Illuminator the Radiance' (apposition) is also defensible, but the verbal-relative reading better preserves the dynamic correspondential character of the Lycopolitan root.

Translated 'gird yourselves' (cf. accumulated ⲍⲁⲕ ⲧⲏⲛⲉ 'gird yourselves'). ⲍⲉⲥⲧ may be Lyc. variant on ⲍⲱⲥⲧ̄ (Greek ζώννυμι 'gird'); paraenetic exhortation context (cf. Eph 6:14, 1 Pet 1:13) confirms.

Translated 'and they pay honor (as tribute) upon the face of the Enemy.' Reading ⲣ̄-ⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲉ as Lyc. variant of ⲣ̄-ⲧⲁⲓⲟ 'be honored / give honor.' Context (souls locked outside the gate of Life, falling under the Enemy) supports the captive-tribute reading: souls become a forced offering of honor to their captor. Alternative reading 'and they become a (judicial) kind/category' (ⲧⲁⲓⲉ = 'kind') also possible.
